title: Creamy Garlic Mushroom Chicken

ingredients.item: red pepper flakes, as many as you like
onions, diced (optional, in addition to the onions below)
chicken breast, cut into small cubes
cooking cream (or twice as much coconut milk/cream)
jalapeños, chopped (at least) — swap for bell pepper, or omit for less heat
butter or ghee, for the pan
cashews or walnuts, for the rice
kewpie mayo mixed with truffle mayo, as a fry sauce (optional)

instructions.text: Combine the curry powder, paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, turmeric, black pepper, salt, a generous amount of olive oil, and pepper flakes to taste. Stir in diced onions if using.
Toss the chicken cubes in the marinade to coat.
Heat a pan over medium heat. Add the chicken only once the pan is sizzling — if it's not hot enough yet, take the chicken back out and wait. Don't let the pan get too hot either.

Cook 2-4 minutes per side depending on thickness, flipping each piece individually so none are missed, and being careful not to overcook. Work in multiple batches if the pan isn't big enough — don't stack the chicken.
Remove the chicken and set aside.
In the same pan over the same heat, add butter or ghee. Add the whole garlic cloves and cook about a minute on each side.
Add the onions, chopped mushrooms, diced garlic, and jalapeños (if using). If you forgot the whole garlic cloves earlier, add them in now too.
Stir in the Dijon mustard, soy sauce, flour, and steak sauce if using. Let simmer 2-3 minutes per side for a little browning.
Return the chicken to the pan, then add the broth cubes mixed with about 1 glass (250-300ml) of water, plus the cooking cream (or coconut milk).
Mix well and simmer 10-20 minutes — the longer it simmers, the thicker and creamier it gets. Periodically check the bottom of the pan for sticking or burning; turn off the heat if it starts to catch.
Serve in separate bowls next to fries and rice topped with nuts, raisins, and/or pickles, plus a drink.
For the fries, try a kewpie mayo and truffle mayo mix as a dipping sauce.

notes: Makes about 10 medium servings or 6 large ones. When serving, feel free to squeeze a slice of lemon over the chicken.

title: Tony Roma's Ribs
prepTime: 20 min active + marinate overnight (at least 7 hrs)
cookTime: about 3 hr 40 min (3 hr bake + basting + 10 min final blast)

ingredients.item: chili powder (leave out if kids are eating)
baby back ribs or spare ribs

instructions.text: Combine the rub ingredients in a bowl and mix well.
The night before the ribs are to be served, coat both sides of the ribs well with the rub and place them in a zip-lock bag in the refrigerator.
Remove the ribs from the fridge at least 7 hours before serving, and coat well with the rub once again.
Combine all sauce ingredients in a medium saucepan over high heat and whisk until smooth.
Bring the sauce to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 30-40 minutes, or until the sauce has thickened. (A store-bought Korean BBQ sauce, e.g. BiBiGo, works as a shortcut instead.)

Preheat the oven to 120°C (225°F is about 108°C — if the ribs are very thick, cook at 150°C instead). Place the ribs fat side up in a shallow, foil-lined baking pan, without a rack, with about 1mm of water in the bottom of the pan.
Bake for 3 hours, topping up the water partway through if the ribs are thick.
After 3 hours, spread BBQ sauce on both sides of the ribs and continue to bake. Add more sauce after another 30 minutes.
Blast at 250°C for 10 minutes to caramelize — do this step last, right before serving.

notes: Serve with corn, broccoli/peas, mashed potato, and baked beans with onions. If making the rub ahead to store dry, leave out the brown sugar and add it fresh when using ("no sugar for dry rib rub"). Adapted from BigOven's "Tony Roma's Ribs" and Carolina Country's "Tony Roma's Blue Ridge Smokies Sauce" (from Todd Wilbur's Top Secret Restaurant Recipes), with handwritten family adjustments to the seasoning amounts, bake time/temp, and technique. One faint note in the margin about a convection-oven temperature (looked like ~140°C) was too hard to make out with confidence — worth checking the original photo.

title: Beef Stroganoff

ingredients.item: beef chuck roast, cut into batons (see instructions)
crème fraîche (½–1 cup), or sour cream
wide egg noodles, buttered, for serving

instructions.text: Cut the beef chuck into steaks about ½–¾ inch thick, then cut those into ½-inch-wide strips (batons). The exact size doesn't matter much as long as the pieces are consistent. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large pan over high heat until shimmering and almost smoking. Add the beef — it's fine to crowd the pan for this cut; the liquid will release and boil off, then the meat will brown in its own juices. Cook until well browned, then transfer to a plate and reserve.

Reduce the heat to medium and add the butter to the same pan — don't wipe it out, you want those browned bits. Add the mushrooms and onion with a big pinch of salt, and sauté until nicely browned; the mushrooms and onions will release liquid that helps deglaze the pan.
Add the garlic and cook, stirring, for about 30 seconds. Add the flour, stir in, and cook for another minute or two.
Add the white wine and about half the beef broth. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom of the pan, until slightly thickened.

Return the beef to the pan along with the rest of the beef broth. Mix well and bring just to a bare simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for about 1 hour, stirring roughly every 20 minutes, until the beef is tender. Add a splash more water or stock if it needs longer or looks dry.
Stir in a generous dollop of crème fraîche (or sour cream) — more for a saucier stroganoff, less for a drier one. Stir in the fresh chives, then taste and adjust salt and pepper.
Serve over buttered wide egg noodles, with a little extra sour cream on top if desired.

notes: Chef John recommends asking your butcher for a piece of chuck from a single muscle, to avoid pieces of membrane or big sections of fat running through it. Homemade crème fraîche is preferred over sour cream, since sour cream can curdle or separate when heated. This is Chef John's "Americanized" (non-traditional) take on stroganoff, with mushrooms and onions served over egg noodles. From Food Wishes: "No Russian, this Beef Stroganoff Recipe" (foodwishes.blogspot.com, March 2011) and its companion YouTube video.

title: Tiramisu
cookTime: overnight to set (or 1 hr freeze + 1 hr fridge if rushed)

ingredients.item: egg yolks (reserve the whites for something else, like a pavlova or pandan chiffon cake)
mascarpone, drained of any excess liquid

instructions.text: Stir the instant coffee and sugar into the hot water until dissolved. Stir in the Amaretto and set aside to cool to room temperature.

Beat the egg yolks and sugar with an electric mixer on medium-high speed until pale, thick, and roughly doubled in volume — this takes about 8-10 minutes. No egg whites are used in this recipe, so skip whipping/folding through any meringue.

Add the drained mascarpone and mix in on low speed just until smooth and combined. Don't overbeat once the mascarpone goes in — over-mixing at this stage can make the cream grainy or cause it to split.
Grease a serving dish (roughly 8-inch/20cm square, or similar) with butter.
Quickly dip each sponge finger into the cooled coffee mixture — a second or two per side is enough, you don't want them turning soggy — and arrange in a single layer in the dish.
Spread half the mascarpone cream evenly over the sponge fingers.
Repeat with a second layer of dipped sponge fingers, then spread the remaining mascarpone cream on top.
Cover and refrigerate overnight for the best texture (or, if short on time, freeze for at least 1 hour then defrost in the fridge for 1 hour — results won't be quite as good as an overnight set).
Sift cocoa powder generously over the top just before serving.

notes: Base recipe is Auntie Siao Siang's recipe as adapted by Michele Anne Lim (28 Oct 1992) — no egg whites/meringue, just yolks. Technique details (long beat time for yolks & sugar, mixing the mascarpone in gently rather than whipping it, quick dip time for the sponge fingers) are drawn from RecipeTinEats' "Easy Tiramisu" and an accompanying video, adapted to skip the egg-white meringue step entirely and to avoid overbeating once the mascarpone is added.

title: Cheesing The Ladder

ingredients.item: broccoli (700g), separated into florets and stems
kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
medium carrot, peeled and finely diced (about 4 oz/120g)
small russet potato, peeled and sliced (about 4 oz/120g)
hot sauce (e.g. Frank's RedHot), a dash

instructions.text: Cut the broccoli florets into bite-sized pieces and set aside. Roughly chop the stems and reserve separately.

Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over high heat until shimmering. Add the broccoli florets and cook without moving until charred on the bottom, about 1 minute. Stir, season with salt and pepper, and continue cooking, stirring occasionally, until tender and charred on several surfaces, about 1 minute longer. Transfer to a rimmed baking sheet to cool.

Return the Dutch oven to medium heat and add the butter, onion, carrot, and broccoli stems. Season with salt and pepper and cook, stirring frequently, until tender but not browned, about 5 minutes, lowering the heat if necessary. Add the garlic and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 30 seconds.

Add the water (or chicken stock), milk, and potato, and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce to a bare simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until the broccoli stems and potato are completely tender, about 30 minutes.

Toss both cheeses together with the mustard powder in a large bowl. Using an immersion blender (or working in batches with a countertop blender), blend the soup, adding the cheese mixture a handful at a time until completely smooth.
Stir in the hot sauce and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Stir in the reserved broccoli florets and pulse with the blender a few more times, until a few pieces are broken down but most bite-sized pieces still remain. Serve immediately.

notes: Broccoli cheddar soup, pulled from a PDF titled "Cheesing The Ladder." Servings are an estimate — the yield wasn't specified in the source. Pairs well with garlic bread and pan-seared chicken or pork on the side.

ingredients.item: chicken stock cube (1/3 of a cube)

instructions.text: Combine the light soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, crushed garlic, and white pepper. Coat the butterflied chicken legs in the marinade.
Pan-fry the marinated chicken over medium heat until golden brown and cooked through on both sides. Set aside.

In the same pan, melt the butter and stir in the black pepper and chicken stock cube. Add the flour and stir to form a paste, then gradually whisk in the water and dark soy sauce. Simmer until thickened into a gravy.
Plate the chicken chop, pour the gravy over it, and serve with french fries, baked beans, mixed vegetables, and dinner rolls or bread.

title: Mapo Tofu

ingredients.group: Dao Kou La Jiao (chili oil topping)
ingredients.item: dried red chilies, cut into 1/2-inch pieces (10-12)

ingredients.group: Dao Kou La Jiao (chili oil topping)

ingredients.item: soft tofu, cut into bite-sized cubes
scallions, diced, white and green parts kept separate

instructions.group: Make the Dao Kou La Jiao
instructions.text: Toast the dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns in a wok over medium-low heat for a couple of minutes. Let cool, then blend until fine. This "peppers under the blade" mix is useful for any ma la (spicy and numbing) dish.

Blend the Doubanjiang, fermented black beans, prawn paste, and cooking wine in a blender until it forms a fine paste. Set aside — this grinds down the broad bean pieces so the texture and flavor come out better.

Cut the tofu into bite-sized cubes. Add the salt to the water and bring to a boil. Blanch the tofu for a couple of minutes, then remove and set aside. This reduces the beany taste and helps the tofu hold together while stirring later.
Heat the wok over high heat until smoking hot. Add the vegetable oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the ground meat and stir until cooked through.
Push the meat to the side. Add the doubanjiang paste and stir over low heat for a couple of minutes to activate the umami flavor.
Add the garlic, ginger, white part of the scallions, paprika, sugar, and half of the Dao Kou La Jiao (reserve the other half for garnish). Stir until well combined and fragrant.

Pour in the beef stock and bring to a boil. Taste and adjust with soy sauce — it should be saltier than usual since the tofu doesn't carry much flavor on its own and this is meant to be eaten with rice.
Add the tofu and simmer on low heat for 5 minutes.
Mix the cornstarch and water into a slurry. Add it to the wok in 3 batches, stirring gently each time to thicken the sauce without breaking the tofu.
Sprinkle the reserved Dao Kou La Jiao and the green part of the scallions on top. Serve with white rice.

notes: From Souped Up Recipes (YouTube), "BETTER THAN TAKEOUT - Mapo Tofu Recipe": https://youtu.be/g9DNcb7cs2s. An authentic mapo tofu should hit 8 characteristics: 麻辣鲜香嫩滑翠整 — numbing, spicy, umami, fragrant, tender, smooth, green (scallion/garlic sprout garnish), and whole (no broken tofu).

title: Haemul-pajeon (Korean Seafood Scallion Pancake)

ingredients.item: green onions, trimmed to the length of your pan
mixed seafood (shrimp, squid, clams), chopped (about 4oz/115g total)

instructions.text: Combine the dark soy sauce, apple cider vinegar, gochugaru, chopped green onion, and toasted sesame seeds in a small bowl. No need to stir until serving — just set aside.
Combine the chopped shrimp, squid, and clams in a bowl (about 1/2 cup / 4oz total). Season with a pinch of salt and black pepper and mix.

Whisk together the flour, potato starch (this is what makes the pancake a little crunchy), and salt in a bowl. Add the stock and mix until very runny, almost like water — a thin batter is key, otherwise the pancake will clump together and turn out dense instead of crispy.
Heat a large pan over medium-high heat until hot, then reduce to medium heat. Add about half the oil (2 tbsp) and swirl to coat.

Dip the green onions in the batter to coat, then lay them side by side in the pan, flipping every other one so they alternate direction and cover the pan evenly. Pour any remaining batter over the top and into the gaps.
Scatter the seasoned seafood evenly over the green onions, then the sliced red pepper, then pour the beaten egg over the top.
Cook over medium heat for 6 minutes, occasionally poking gaps between the green onions so the batter spreads and cooks evenly, until the bottom is golden and crisp but not burnt.
Flip the pancake. Drizzle the remaining oil around the edge and tilt the pan so the oil runs underneath — this helps the bottom turn crispy. Cook for another 3 minutes.
Flip once more, raise the heat to medium-high, and cook for 1 more minute to crisp the other side.
Slide onto a plate. Cut into wedges, or snip the green onions with scissors if the pieces are too long to eat whole. Serve with the dipping sauce.

notes: From Maangchi (YouTube), "Haemul-pajeon (Green onion pancake with seafood: 해물파전)": https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bnYr77vOyM0, full recipe also at https://www.maangchi.com/recipe/haemul-pajeon. Recipe is sized for a 12.5-inch pan — halve it for a smaller pan. Maangchi notes fresh oysters make a great addition if you can get them.

title: Traditional Whole Napa Cabbage Kimchi (Tongbaechu-kimchi)
cookTime: 1-2 days to ferment at room temp, then refrigerate

ingredients.item: napa cabbage (1 large head, or 2 smaller ones)
coarse sea salt or kosher salt, for brining
salted fermented shrimp (saeujeot), with its juice
gochugaru, Korean hot pepper flakes (1-2.5 cups, to taste)
Korean radish, cut into thin matchsticks
scallions, a generous amount, cut into 2-inch pieces
Korean chives (buchu) or minari (water dropwort), a handful (optional)

instructions.text: Cut a few inches into the base of the cabbage with a knife, then tear it in half by hand from the slit. If the head is very large, split each half again into quarters.
Briefly soak the cabbage in cold water first — wet leaves absorb salt more evenly. Sprinkle the salt generously between the leaves, using more on the thicker white stem ends.
Let the cabbage sit for about 2 hours total, turning it over every 30 minutes so it salts evenly, until the leaves are wilted and the base is flexible.
Wash the salted cabbage in fresh cold water 2-3 times to remove excess salt, then drain well.

Whisk the water and sweet rice flour together in a small pot and bring to a boil, stirring, until it thickens into a glossy porridge (about a couple of minutes). Stir in the brown sugar until dissolved and shiny, then remove from the heat and let cool completely.
Blend the garlic, ginger, and onion into a smooth puree.

Combine the cooled porridge, the garlic-ginger-onion puree, fish sauce, and salted shrimp (with its juice) in a large bowl. Add the gochugaru — start with about 1 cup for a milder kimchi, up to 2.5 cups for a spicier one — and mix into a paste. Taste and adjust.
Mix the julienned radish, scallions, and chives or minari (if using) into the paste.

Wearing food-safe gloves (recommended if this is your first time — the paste is spicy), spread the paste generously between every leaf of the drained cabbage, working from the base toward the tip so each leaf is coated.

Pack the stuffed cabbage tightly into a large jar or container, pressing down firmly so no air pockets remain and the cabbage is submerged in its own juices. Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds on top and close the lid.

Let it sit at room temperature for 1-2 days. It's ready when it smells sour and the surface starts bubbling — signs that fermentation is active. You can also enjoy it fresh, unfermented, right after mixing.

Once fermented to your taste, move the kimchi to the refrigerator to slow fermentation. Keep it pressed down and submerged in its juices — it will keep improving (and getting more sour) over several weeks.

notes: From Maangchi (YouTube), "Traditional kimchi recipe (Tongbaechu-kimchi: 통배추김치)": https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eTucCw1w6Ak, full recipe also at https://www.maangchi.com/recipe/tongbaechu-kimchi. Also called baechu-kimchi or pogi-kimchi — this is the classic whole-leaf napa cabbage kimchi most people just call "kimchi." Radish, scallion, and chive/minari amounts are flexible — go by feel.

title: Chicken Parmesan

ingredients.item: can whole San Marzano tomatoes (or 2 lb fresh tomatoes, blanched, peeled, and chopped)
kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

instructions.text: Sauté the chopped onion in oil for about 3 minutes, then add the garlic for 30 seconds. Add the tomato paste and chili flakes and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, crushing them as you stir. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, then lower the heat to keep a gentle bubble.
Add the oregano, basil stems, and water. Stir and simmer for 45 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper. Remove the basil stems and keep the sauce warm.
Place each breast between sheets of plastic wrap and pound it flat with a mallet. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Set up three stations: flour seasoned with pepper, garlic powder, oregano, and basil; beaten eggs mixed with a little flour; and panko mixed with the pre-grated Parmesan.
Dredge each breast in flour, then egg, then panko, using one hand for dry and the other for wet. For an extra-crispy coating, dip in egg and panko a second time. Rest until ready to fry.
Heat the peanut oil to 350°F (175°C). Fry the chicken for about 5 minutes, until deep golden brown. Drain on paper towels.
Set the chicken on a wire rack over a rimmed baking sheet. Top with fresh basil, mozzarella, and grated Parmesan, then broil briefly until the cheese melts and turns lightly golden.
Boil the pasta. Meanwhile, warm a few ladles of sauce in a saucepan over medium heat.
When the pasta is about a minute from done and the sauce is bubbling, add the pasta and 1/4 cup of pasta water to the sauce and finish cooking.
Turn off the heat and stir in chopped basil, grated Parmesan, and butter until combined.
Plate the pasta, top with the fried chicken, then add more sauce, Parmesan, and chopped basil.

notes: From Basics with Babish (YouTube), "Chicken Parmesan | Basics with Babish": https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZrR0VbqNdW8, full recipe also at https://www.babi.sh/basicsepisodes/chicken-parmesan. Double-dipping the chicken in egg and panko gives a crispier crust. Tools: meat mallet, frying thermometer, wire rack over a rimmed baking sheet.

title: Yoke Chung

ingredients.item: white pepper and salt, to taste
tapioca flour (add when ready to fry)
spring onion, chopped (same volume as the pork)

instructions: Marinate the pork with the Shaoxing wine, light and dark soy sauce, sugar, white pepper, and salt.
When about to fry, add the tapioca flour and mix well.
Fry the pork until half cooked.
Add the spring onion and fry until everything is cooked through.
notes: From PorPor Helen's mum. Use the same volume of chopped spring onion as pork — this is what adds sweetness to the dish.

title: Mama's Zhap Hueh
instructions: Fry the chopped garlic, reserving some of the fried garlic for garnish.
Sear the pork belly with the garlic.
Add water to cover and simmer until the pork is tender.
At the end, add the pork balls (if using) and the cabbage, stems first, and simmer until tender.
Serve garnished with coriander and the reserved fried garlic.
notes: Mum's Chap Huay recipe, written down 5 November 2022. No amounts given — go by feel.
